newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Waigel says EMU stability pact not negotiable.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says EMU stability pact not negotiable.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Monday stressed the importance of budget discipline and stable prices and said the stability pact aimed at creating a solid basis for Europe's planned single currency was not up for discussion.
"What has been agreed upon and discussed for two years can no longer be put up for negotiation," he said after a meeting of European Union economic and finance ministers in Luxembourg.

Waigel said none of the delegations had called for reopening talks on the stability pact, which outlines a range of punitive sanctions should EMU participants fail to maintain budget discipline after the euro is introduced in 1999.

"No renegotiation of the stability pact is being demanded," he said, but added that France wanted additional elements on employment policy to be included in the so-called Maastricht II treaty to be agreed at the EU summit in Amsterdam.
The French side has yet to define what its position is on the stability pact, Waigel said, but added that Germany could and would listen to that position.
"But there will be no change in our policy," Waigel said, adding that economic convergence between EU members was decisive for the launch and continuation of monetary union.
Waigel said he saw no chance of reaching final agreement on the stability pact before the Amsterdam summit of EU leaders.
He stressed that handling unemployment would remain a national responsibility as Europe moves closer together.
